must_remember: Wavefronts of a plane wave are flat, parallel planes perpendicular to the propagation vector $\mathbf{k}$.
The phase velocity of a plane wave is given by $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \nu \lambda$.
Maximum particle velocity in a harmonic plane wave is $v_{p,\text{max}} = A\omega$, which is distinct from wave velocity.
Intensity of a plane wave is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude and square of the frequency ($I \propto A^2 \nu^2$).
Ideal plane waves do not suffer geometric attenuation; their amplitude remains constant across planes perpendicular to propagation.

glossary.meaning: A vector whose magnitude is $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$ and whose direction indicates the direction of wave propagation.
The speed at which a point of constant phase of the wave propagates through the medium, given by $v = \frac{\omega}{k}$.
The instantaneous transverse or longitudinal speed of a medium element about its equilibrium position, given by $v_p = \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}$.
The product of medium density $\rho$ and wave speed $v$, expressed as $Z = \rho v$ for plane acoustic waves.
The average power transmitted per unit area normal to the direction of wave propagation.
